proposal: The Mandate recommends that FRA modernize its inspection rules: adopt a technology-based track inspection program in place of 50-year-old requirements, and take final action on a rulemaking that would track brake inspections electronically instead of with paper air brake slips, extending brake inspection intervals and easing restrictions on adding or removing blocks of cars. It also criticizes planned FRA proposals on dispatcher and signal employee certification and on emergency escape breathing apparatus.

status_summary: The electronic air brake slip rulemaking that the Mandate refers to, proposed on 2021-01-15, has no later Federal Register action found. FRA instead proposed brake system amendments on 2025-07-01 (90 FR 28660) and published a final rule on 2026-08-31 (91 FR 55779), effective 2026-09-30, which writes long-standing locomotive and passenger equipment brake waivers into regulation, allows an electronic maintenance record for passenger equipment and sets a 184-day verification interval for digital air flow indicators used in freight Class I brake tests. It does not mention air brake slips and does not change freight train air brake test intervals more broadly or block-of-cars restrictions. No track inspection modernization rule was found; a May 2025 notice published a railroad industry petition for waiver of track inspection rules.

timeline.event: FRA published a proposed rule amending brake system maintenance and inspection requirements.
FRA published the final brake rule, which includes codified waivers and longer intervals for certain equipment.
The final brake rule took effect.

title: Modernize FRA brake and track inspection requirements
uncertainties: The final brake rule (91 FR 55779) was read on federalregister.gov in review on 2026-10-18 and by the researcher; the proposed rule (90 FR 28660) was read by the researcher. Neither mentions air brake slips or blocks of cars; electronic records appear only in the passenger equipment section. Federal Register API term searches found no action on the electronic air brake slip proposal after 2021 and, since 2025-01-20, only waiver petition notices touching track inspection; a 2025-11-19 notice of a BNSF petition to extend a track inspection waiver was seen in an API listing but its page returned a server error, so it was not added as an event. Term searches can miss titles, and FRA waiver decisions are docketed outside the Federal Register. The status of the dispatcher certification and breathing apparatus proposals was not checked. The 2026 rule is a related brake modernization step, not the specific proceeding the Mandate names.
